lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Outline a two-minute speech with timed boxes and one memorable line.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: Realistic timing; line is quotable and on-thesis.

CHECK
Writing an essay and reading it unchanged. Speeches need oral shaping.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Draft a full speech for a school-safe issue; mark timing and highlight the memorable line.

Write a short reflection describing one specific revision you made and why.

lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Draft a full speech for a school-safe issue; mark timing and highlight the memorable line. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Original response on new material: Strong answer: Realistic timing; line is quotable and on-thesis. Reasoning: I used speech draft by attending to register rather than copying the worked model.

Parent: Written model 2: Common error: Writing an essay and reading it unchanged. Speeches need oral shaping. Correction: Strong answer: Realistic timing; line is quotable and on-thesis. Why: the correction restores accurate use of speech draft.

Parent: Likely misconception: Writing an essay and reading it unchanged. Speeches need oral shaping. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Produce a fresh example demonstrating speech draft on new material (not the worked model). Explain the particular words, sources or choices that make it work.

teach_steps.explain:
Writing a speech drafts for the ear: shorter sentences, spoken register, timed sections and one memorable line that carries the thesis. Practise with a clock.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make decisions based on specific language evidence, rather than guess or copy someone else. Keep the meaning accurate and explain the choice.

HOW TO WORK
Read the original example and locate the words or actions that support the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Check your response against the feedback: did you address the same skill and show your reasoning? If a detail is uncertain, identify what would have to be checked. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than making the answer longer.
